cup: Extreme close shot, looking across a single chipped off-white enamel mug with a dark rim, abandoned on the weathered wooden sill inside an old lighthouse. The mug sits in the left-middle of frame. In the tea we see a fine concentric disturbance from the keeper's signal. Tall rain-streaked window behind, storm-blue sea out through vintage glass, warm amber lamp reflection on the right, some drops shimmering on the wooden sill. No hands, no person, no letters. Atmospheric still life, clear silhouette of the mug, a dramatically different viewpoint from the other scenes.
lens: An abstractly beautiful EXTREME MACRO inside a rotating lighthouse optical lantern: concentric stepped FRESNEL GLASS rings cut the frame in huge arcs, their amber core just off center to the left is surrounded by engraved teal, bottle-green and gold ridges. You can see tiny salt crystals and refractions of the sea in the beehive lens; a thin dark brass strut intersects the edge, with fiery vermilion light leaks. Pure analog optical beauty with circles that can match-cut to a whale eye or a droplet. Real handcrafted glass installation, no person or lettering.
